answer: An agent claims one identity per orchard it instruments, submitting signed dew-point readings from sensors hung on a trellis row and two nearby rows. An atlas of microclimate maps confirms the orchard's cooling curve, a walnut-shell sensor housing holds the tamper-evident key, and the ivory-coloured dawn frost must appear on all three sensors together, so one operator cannot mint many identities from one orchard without the readings collapsing into identical copies.
